name: Rhode Island
overview: In Rhode Island, each city or town tax collector can advertise and sell real estate with unpaid taxes at a collector's sale. The buyer gets a tax title that can still be redeemed at any time before a petition to foreclose the right of redemption is filed. That petition can be brought after one year from the sale. To redeem from a private buyer, the owner pays the purchase price plus interest at one percent per month, costs and a penalty; when the city or town itself bought the property, the penalty is ten percent of the purchase price within six months of the sale, plus one percent for each later month.

overview_sources.quote: The collector may advertise and take, or sell any real estate liable for taxes in the manner directed.
at any time prior to the filing of the petition for foreclosure
After one year from a sale of land for taxes
at the rate of one percent (1%) per month
a penalty which shall be ten percent (10%) of the purchase price if redeemed within six (6) months
an additional one percent (1%) of the purchase price for each succeeding month

counties.office: Tax Collector (Tax Office), Town of West Greenwich
counties.address: Town Hall, 280 Victory Highway, West Greenwich, RI 02817
counties.next_sale_note: No tax sale date is posted on the Town's site; the Tax Office FAQ explains how its tax sale auction works but gives no schedule.
counties.how_to_bid: Per the Town's Tax Office FAQ: each bidder fills out the registration form required by Rhode Island law, stating resident or non-resident status, signed and notarized; proper identification is required and bidders must be at least 18. Lots are auctioned in the order they appear on the tax sale list. Each winning bidder pays the full amount within one hour after the auction ends, in cash or cashier's check, covering the Town's outstanding taxes plus interest and legal costs. The buyer receives a collector's deed subject to the right of redemption; the Tax Collector executes deeds within 60 days of the sale and records them. Parcels are sold as is, and the Tax Collector may cancel the sale up to the time of sale. Deposit: not stated. Redemption period: not stated on the FAQ.
